name: Karst
desc: A cave system dissolves itself into limestone in cross-section — water sinks through a fabric of vertical joints and bedding planes, and because a wider fissure takes more flow it widens faster and captures its neighbours, so a few conduits win and open into passages; the water table falls over minutes, strands the tube it cut, and starts a new one below it, while the drained tiers above grow dripstone.

energy.doc: dissolution vigour (how fast conduits open) + colour/contrast gain

scale.doc: magnification into the section around x/y — 1 shows the whole massif, 2.6 crops to a single passage

speed.doc: rate of cave genesis and base-level cycling

density.doc: recharge — number of water parcels, i.e. how densely the network is explored

joints.doc: fracture fabric: 0 = near-massive rock, few slow conduits; 1 = a heavily jointed and bedded massif that opens into a maze

hue.doc: limestone hue anchor; rotates the plate with it

x.doc: view centre x (only bites when scale > 1)

y.doc: view centre y (only bites when scale > 1)

style.doc: aesthetic: survey = cave-survey plate, buff bedded limestone, blue phreatic water, cream dripstone; xray = abstracted negative, the rock vanishes and only the void network glows; thermal = false-colour; ink = sumi tonal wash
